newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Treasury, not banks, must handle budget cash-Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: Treasury, not banks, must handle budget cash-Yeltsin.

text.p: Russia's Treasury, not commercial banks, should handle distribution of budget funds, President Boris Yeltsin has said in a written address to parliament, an advance copy of which was obtained by Reuters on Wednesday.
"All budget expenditures and revenues must go through a single account in the Federal Treasury," the document said.
The president is expected to address a joint assembly of the two chambers of parliament at 11 a.m (0800 GMT) on Thursday.
Yeltsin ordered the government to set up Treasury branches across Russia to handle budget funds next year.
Under the current system, budget funds are channelled to territories and regions through authorised banks.
Competition for the right to handle budget money is high and critics have said the system is poorly controlled and prone to corruption.
Yeltsin also said that Russia should use international accounting standards when drawing up a federal budget.
Unused budget funds should be placed in the Central Bank, or in what Yeltsin called "absolutely reliable" commercial banks to earn interest.
Yeltsin also ordered the government to develop a tender system in which state orders for goods, work or services would be contracted out on a competitive basis.
